issues.t: Targa roof leaks water
issues.sym: Water dripping onto the seats or floor in rain or a car wash, damp carpets, a musty smell, and extra wind noise from the roof.
issues.why: The removable targa top relies on rubber seals that shrink and harden with age. The front seal is the usual culprit; a top that is not adjusted properly makes it worse.
issues.next: Dry the carpets out quickly to stop rust and mold. Have the roof fit adjusted and the seals treated with silicone grease; badly worn seals, especially the front one, need replacing.

issues.t: Clogged rear window drains: water sloshing
issues.sym: You hear water sloshing behind the seats when you turn, and find water in the trunk or on the rear strut towers.
issues.why: Rain that gets past the rear window collects in a tray under it and is meant to run out through drain tubes on each side. When the tubes clog, the water sits there and rusts the body.
issues.next: Clear the drains soon. A shop or handy owner removes the rear trim panels and a metal cover to reach the tubes at the bottom of each side.

issues.t: Rust on rear wheel arches and rocker panels
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or holes around the rear wheel arches, quarter panels, rocker panels under the side skirts, or the trunk floor.
issues.why: Water from roof and drain leaks plus road salt attack the rear of the body. Rust can also form under the pedals and behind the front pillar seals, which is more serious.
issues.next: Check under the side skirts and carpets. Small arch rust can be cut out and patched; rust in structural areas needs a body shop opinion.

issues.t: No start when hot from a failing main relay
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, often after it has been driven and parked, and you don't hear the fuel pump hum when you switch on the key.
issues.why: Hondas of this era use a main relay under the dash that powers the fuel pump. Its solder joints crack with heat, so it cuts out when warm.
issues.next: Have a shop test fuel pump power while the problem is happening. A new main relay (or a re-soldered one) is a common fix; also check the engine ground wires.

issues.t: Distributor failure: stalling, misfire or no spark
issues.sym: Stalling, misfiring, a check engine light, or an engine that cranks with no spark. You may hear grinding or clicking from the distributor.
issues.why: The distributor holds the ignition coil, igniter and bearings, and these parts commonly fail around 60,000 miles or later. One owner went through three in six months.
issues.next: Have the trouble codes read and a spark test done. If the distributor is at fault, replace it with a quality unit and have the ignition timing set.

issues.t: Oil leaking from the distributor seal
issues.sym: Oil on the back of the engine near the distributor and a light burning-oil smell.
issues.why: The O-ring and seal where the distributor plugs into the cylinder head harden and leak.
issues.next: Replace the distributor O-ring and seal. Oil getting inside the distributor can also cause ignition faults.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil leak
issues.sym: Oil seeping around the top of the engine, a burning smell after driving, or oil in the spark plug wells.
issues.why: The rubber valve cover gasket hardens with age and heat, which is common on higher-mileage engines.
issues.next: Replace the valve cover gasket and spark plug tube seals together.

issues.t: VTEC solenoid gasket leak
issues.sym: Oil on the side of the engine near the VTEC solenoid, and sometimes a check engine light for the VTEC system.
issues.why: The gasket under the VTEC solenoid hardens and leaks. If oil gets low or the screen under the solenoid clogs, VTEC may stop engaging.
issues.next: Replace the solenoid gasket and clean its screen. Keep the oil level full, since VTEC relies on oil pressure.

issues.t: Timing belt overdue: risk of major engine damage
issues.sym: Usually no warning. If the belt snaps the engine dies while driving and won't restart.
issues.why: All del Sol engines use a rubber timing belt and are interference engines, so a broken belt lets the pistons hit the valves.
issues.next: If you have no record of a recent change, replace the timing belt, tensioner and water pump now. Honda's schedule is about every 60,000 to 100,000 miles depending on engine, or roughly 7 years.

issues.t: Worn engine mounts: vibration and clunks
issues.sym: Vibration through the steering wheel and seats, rattling from the dash, and a clunk when shifting or pulling away.
issues.why: The rubber engine mounts crack and collapse with age. RepairPal lists bad engine mounts as a common del Sol problem.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected while someone shifts between Drive and Reverse with the brake on. Replace the broken ones.

issues.t: CV joint clicking on turns
issues.sym: A clicking or knocking noise when turning sharply, especially in a parking lot. Grease may be spattered inside the wheel.
issues.why: A split CV boot lets grease out and dirt in, and the outer CV joint wears.
issues.next: Check the CV boots. A torn boot caught early can be replaced; a clicking joint needs a new axle.

issues.t: Manual gearbox grinds going into 2nd or 3rd
issues.sym: A grind or crunch when shifting into 2nd or 3rd, mostly on fast shifts.
issues.why: The synchros that match gear speeds wear out, most often on 2nd and 3rd.
issues.next: Try fresh Honda manual transmission fluid first. If grinding continues, the gearbox needs a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: Clutch slipping or not releasing
issues.sym: Engine revs rise without the car speeding up, the clutch engages very high or near the floor, or the car creeps in gear with the pedal down.
issues.why: The clutch is a wear item, and older cars often have a worn clutch, a dragging release bearing or old clutch fluid.
issues.next: Have the clutch fluid and hydraulics checked. A slipping clutch needs replacing before it fails completely.

issues.t: Heater fan only works on some speeds
issues.sym: The fan works only on high, or not on the lower settings.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor behind the glovebox commonly burns out on cars with the 4-speed fan switch.
issues.next: Replace the blower motor resistor. If the fan doesn't work on any speed, have the motor and wiring tested.

issues.t: A/C not cooling (compressor failure)
issues.sym: Warm air from the vents with the A/C on, sometimes with a noise from the compressor.
issues.why: On cars this age the A/C compressor is a common culprit, not just low refrigerant.
issues.next: Have a leak check and pressure test done before paying for a recharge.

issues.t: Targa top rattles and squeaks
issues.sym: Rattles or squeaks from the roof, often between the top and the crossbar near the third brake light.
issues.why: The roof panel and its seals wear and shrink, so the panel can move against the body.
issues.next: Have the roof latches adjusted and the seals cleaned and lubricated with silicone grease.

issues.t: Power windows slow or off track
issues.sym: A door window or the power rear window moves slowly, stops partway, or tilts in the frame.
issues.why: Window regulators and their guides wear out; owners report windows coming off their tracks.
issues.next: Test every window, including the rear one. A worn regulator gets replaced.

issues.t: Inside door handle breaks
issues.sym: The inside door handle snaps or goes slack and won't open the door.
issues.why: The plastic handle breaks where the lock rod attaches.
issues.next: Replace the handle. Until then, make sure everyone can still get out, since the door may only open from outside.

issues.t: Parking brake doesn't hold
issues.sym: The car rolls on a slope with the parking brake on, or the lever pulls up very high.
issues.why: Stretched or seized parking brake cables, and one owner reported a snapped cable.
issues.next: Park in gear and on level ground until fixed. Have the cables and rear brakes adjusted or replaced.

issues.t: Check engine light with misfire codes
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes on and off, with misfire codes P0301 to P0304, and a rough run.
issues.why: Honda issued bulletins on the check engine light and misfire codes for this car. Worn plugs, wires, the distributor or ignition parts are the usual causes.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If the light flashes, ease off and get it checked soon, because heavy misfires can damage the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Twang noise from the front suspension
issues.sym: A twang or ping from the front when going over bumps or turning.
issues.why: Honda issued a bulletin for a twang noise that sounds like the coil spring moving against its seat.
issues.next: Have a shop inspect the spring seats and strut mounts for the bulletin's fix.

issues.t: Water leak in a car wash
issues.sym: Water inside the car after a car wash even if rain doesn't usually get in.
issues.why: Honda issued a bulletin about water leaking in during car washes, where high-pressure water gets past body seals.
issues.next: Ask a Honda dealer about the bulletin and have the leaking seal found with a water test.
